$comment: ENGINE-WIDE defaults for the spec pass. These were literals inside spec-mode-runner.js, changeable only by editing a 9,000-line script. An operator overrides any of them per run with the environment variable named beside each.

toolCalls.$comment: How much an agent may LOOK before it must answer — the most consequential number in the spec pass. Live 2026-08-08 a survey told to open three repositories ran out of calls, reported 'no existing infrastructure, this is greenfield work' about a brownfield estate with 243 matching source files in the first codeline, and a roster was minted on that verdict.
toolCalls.$perCodelineSurveyNote: Multiplied by the number of codelines in scope. A single ceiling cannot serve both an agent looking at one repository and a survey instructed to open every repository in the estate.

perSeam.$comment: Seams that deliberately differ from perAgent. The detective converges by iterating; the PRD change reviewer answers a narrow question.

tools.$comment: The read-only builtin floor granted to every spec-mode agent. Kept here rather than derived as 'every safe builtin' because fetch_url is also safe, and granting network access to the spec pass is a separate decision that must be made deliberately. Plugin tools are NOT listed: they are derived from each codeline's .epam/settings.json, so a codeline provisioned with the codegraph plugin grants codegraph_query automatically.

promptTrim.$comment: How much accumulated coordinator guidance an agent keeps. Live 2026-08-09 a writer's prompt hit 53366 chars against this threshold and was trimmed to the most recent sections — two thirds of its guidance discarded, with a WARNING the only trace. The section count replaced a 1 on 2026-07-11, after a run repeated an identical mistake five retries after being told not to, because a newer heading had pushed the earlier diagnosis out of a single-heading window.
